new_quiz.q: What is a material in Unreal Engine?
choices: The asset that decides how a surface looks
The asset that stores the shape of a mesh
The asset that holds the lights of a level
The asset that plays an animation
new_quiz.explain: A material decides the color of a surface, how shiny it is, and if it is metal. Every surface in Unreal has one.

new_quiz.q: How do you build a material in the Material Editor?
choices: You paint on the mesh with a brush
You type the values into the Outliner
You connect nodes to the inputs of the material
You import a finished material from an image
new_quiz.explain: The Material Editor is a graph. Small boxes called nodes hold values, and you connect them to inputs such as Base Color.

new_quiz.q: How do you open the Material Editor for M_Basic?
choices: Drag M_Basic into the level
Double-click M_Basic in the Content Browser
Press F9 while M_Basic is selected
Open Window, then Output Log
new_quiz.explain: Double-clicking a material asset opens it in the Material Editor, where you see its graph and a preview.

new_quiz.q: What does a Constant3Vector node hold?
choices: A texture
One number
A mesh
A color
new_quiz.explain: A Constant3Vector holds three numbers, which are used as red, green and blue. You connect it to Base Color.

new_quiz.q: Which node do you connect to Roughness and to Metallic?
choices: A Constant node, which holds one number
A Constant3Vector node, which holds a color
A Text Render node, which holds a text
A Timeline node, which holds a curve
new_quiz.explain: Roughness and Metallic each need a single number. A Constant node holds exactly one number.

new_quiz.q: What do the instruction counts in the Stats panel show?
choices: How many meshes use the material
How many times the material was saved
How much work the material costs to draw
How large the material file is on disk
new_quiz.explain: More instructions mean more work for the graphics card on every pixel. The Stats panel lets you watch this number while you build.

new_quiz.q: What happens to a surface when you change Roughness from 1 to 0?
choices: It becomes transparent
It becomes smooth and shows sharp reflections
It becomes darker in color
It becomes matte and dull
new_quiz.explain: Roughness 0 is a smooth surface that reflects like a mirror. Roughness 1 is fully rough and looks matte.

new_quiz.q: Which input of the material decides if the surface is metal?
choices: Base Color
Roughness
Emissive Color
Metallic
new_quiz.explain: Metallic is 0 for surfaces that are not metal and 1 for metal. Base Color and Roughness then decide the color and the shine.

new_quiz.q: What does PBR stand for?
choices: Pixel based reflection
Physically based rendering
Projected bump rendering
Painted base roughness
new_quiz.explain: PBR means physically based rendering. It describes a surface with a few inputs that act like real materials do.

new_quiz.q: What is a dielectric?
choices: Any material that is a polished metal
Any material that gives off light
Any material that is not a metal
Any material that is transparent
new_quiz.explain: Dielectric is the word for surfaces that are not metal, such as plastic, wood or stone. In a material, their Metallic value is 0.

new_quiz.q: What is the gain of plausible PBR values?
choices: The surface looks right under any light
The surface needs no textures
The surface is drawn without any cost
The surface casts no shadows
new_quiz.explain: Values that match real materials react to light like those materials. You do not need to fix the surface again for each new lighting setup.

new_quiz.q: Which Base Color values should you avoid on your swatches?
choices: Gray values
Warm colors
Cool colors
Pure black and pure white
new_quiz.explain: No real surface is pure black or pure white. Such values break the lighting, so you keep Base Color in a plausible range.

new_quiz.q: Which values describe the polished metal swatch?
choices: Metallic 0 and a high Roughness
Metallic 1 and a high Roughness
Metallic 1 and a low Roughness
Metallic 0 and a low Roughness
new_quiz.explain: Metallic 1 makes the surface a metal. A low Roughness makes it smooth, so it looks polished.

new_quiz.q: What is a normal map?
choices: A texture that fakes small bumps on the surface
A texture that stores the color of the surface
A map of the level seen from above
A list of the materials on a mesh
new_quiz.explain: A normal map changes how light hits each pixel, so a flat surface seems to have small bumps. The mesh itself does not change.

new_quiz.q: How do you recognize the normal maps in the folder Characters/Mannequins/Textures of the template?
choices: Their names start with M_
Their names end in _N
Their names end in _D
Their names start with SM_
new_quiz.explain: The normal maps of the template have names that end in _N. A naming rule like this tells you the kind of texture without opening it.

new_quiz.q: Why do you place the four spheres next to each other in one level?
choices: So they share one material
So they can be selected with one click
So the level needs only one label
So they are all under the same light
new_quiz.explain: Under the same light, any difference you see comes from the materials. That makes the comparison fair.

new_quiz.q: What does it mean when a material samples a texture?
choices: The material deletes the image after use
The material paints a new image
The material reads the image
The material saves the image to disk
new_quiz.explain: Textures are images. A material samples, or reads, them to get detail such as color or bumps.

new_quiz.q: What are UVs?
choices: The coordinates that place the image on the mesh
The two brightest colors of a texture
The settings that compress a texture
The lights that shine on a mesh
new_quiz.explain: UVs connect the flat image to the 3D surface. Changing them moves, scales or rotates the texture on the mesh.

new_quiz.q: What is a packed texture?
choices: A texture that was compressed into a ZIP file
A texture that stores a different grayscale map in each color channel
A texture that holds several animation frames
A texture that is used by more than one mesh
new_quiz.explain: The red, green and blue channels each hold their own grayscale map. One file then does the work of three, which saves memory.

new_quiz.q: Why are wrong texture settings a common problem?
choices: The editor crashes when a setting is wrong
The texture is deleted when a setting is wrong
The material refuses to compile
Unreal does not show an error, and the surface just looks a little wrong
new_quiz.explain: Nothing warns you about a wrong setting. You only notice it if you know how the surface should look, so you check the settings of each texture.

new_quiz.q: Which sRGB setting is right for the packed texture T_Quinn_01_MRA?
choices: On, because every texture needs sRGB
On, because it has three channels
Off, because its channels hold data and not color
Off, because it is smaller than the color texture
new_quiz.explain: sRGB is for images that are seen as color, such as T_Quinn_01_D. The channels of a packed texture are plain numbers, so sRGB must be off.

new_quiz.q: What does the tiling parameter on the TexCoord node change?
choices: How many times the texture repeats on the mesh
How bright the texture is
How many channels the texture has
How strongly the texture is compressed
new_quiz.explain: The TexCoord node gives the UVs to the texture samples. Multiplying them makes the texture repeat more or less often.

new_quiz.q: How do you use one map of the packed texture on its own?
choices: Import the texture three times
Take the single channel pin, such as R, G or B, from its texture sample
Turn on sRGB for the texture
Rotate the UVs by 90 degrees
new_quiz.explain: The texture sample has separate output pins for the channels. Each pin gives one grayscale map that you connect to its own input.

new_quiz.q: On the large floor you can see the texture repeat. How do you fix it?
choices: Delete the normal texture
Set Metallic to 1
Move the mesh to another level
Change the scale or rotate the UVs
new_quiz.explain: A visible repeat comes from the same image tiling in a regular way. A different scale or a rotation of the UVs breaks up the pattern.

new_quiz.q: What is a parameter in a material?
choices: A node that can only hold a texture
A named value that can be changed later without opening the material graph
A comment box around a group of nodes
A setting of the mesh that uses the material
new_quiz.explain: A parameter has a name and a default value. A Material Instance can change it, and nobody has to edit the graph.

new_quiz.q: What is a Material Instance?
choices: A material without any inputs
A backup of the material graph
A texture made from a material
A copy of a material that only changes its parameters
new_quiz.explain: An instance uses the graph of its parent material and only sets parameter values. That makes it fast to create many looks.

new_quiz.q: Which kind of parameter holds a single number, for example for roughness or tiling?
choices: A scalar parameter
A vector parameter
A texture parameter
A group parameter
new_quiz.explain: A scalar parameter is one number. Roughness and tiling each need only one number.

new_quiz.q: Which kind of parameter do you use for a tint color?
choices: A scalar parameter
A texture parameter
A vector parameter
A sort parameter
new_quiz.explain: A color has several channels. A vector parameter holds them together, so it is the right kind for a tint.

new_quiz.q: What does the sort priority of a parameter set?
choices: How fast the parameter is drawn
The order in which the parameters are listed
Which instance may change the parameter
The largest value the parameter may have
new_quiz.explain: Sort priority sets the order of the parameters inside their group. A good order puts the most used values first.

new_quiz.q: Why do you put the parameters in named groups?
choices: So the material needs fewer instructions
So the textures are compressed
So the parameters cannot be changed
So someone else can find them in an instance
new_quiz.explain: An instance lists its parameters by group. Clear group names make the right value easy to find for anyone who opens it.

new_quiz.q: What does a parameter in a Material Instance use until you override it?
choices: The value 0
A random value
The default value from the parent material
The value of the last instance you opened
new_quiz.explain: Each parameter gets a default value in the parent material. The instance keeps that value until you turn on the override for that parameter and set your own.

new_quiz.q: What do parameters and instances let one material do?
choices: Serve many different surfaces
Work without any textures
Replace the lights of the level
Change the shape of a mesh
new_quiz.explain: The same graph can look like many materials when its values change. Three instances with different values give three different looks.

new_quiz.q: What is a landscape in Unreal Engine?
choices: A photo of a sky that lights the scene
A small mesh used for rocks
The large terrain actor used for outdoor ground
A volume that holds fog
new_quiz.explain: A landscape is the terrain actor for outdoor ground. Because the ground fills much of the view outside, its material matters a lot.

new_quiz.q: What does a landscape material hold?
choices: Several layers that you paint onto the terrain
One color that covers the whole terrain
The height of every point of the terrain
The plants that grow on the terrain
new_quiz.explain: A landscape material has layers. With a brush you decide where each layer shows on the terrain.

new_quiz.q: What does the Landscape Layer Blend node do?
choices: It raises and lowers the terrain
It places grass meshes on the terrain
It imports ground textures from Fab
It mixes the layers based on where you paint
new_quiz.explain: The node takes the layers as inputs and gives out one result. Where you painted a layer, that layer is shown.

new_quiz.q: What are layer info objects?
choices: Notes that describe each texture
Small assets that store where each layer is painted
Brushes for sculpting the terrain
Nodes that tile a texture
new_quiz.explain: Each layer needs a layer info object. It stores the painted area of that layer on the landscape.

new_quiz.q: You assigned the material to the landscape, but you cannot paint a layer. What do you check first?
choices: That the level has a Sky Light
That the landscape is larger than the level
That the layer info object for that layer was created
That the textures come from Fab
new_quiz.explain: Without a layer info object, the landscape has no place to store the paint of that layer. You create one for each layer before you paint.

new_quiz.q: From where do you judge the tiling scale of the ground textures?
choices: From the height of a player standing on the ground
From high above the whole landscape
From inside the Material Editor
From under the landscape
new_quiz.explain: The player sees the ground from eye height. From there the texture must be neither too large nor too small.

new_quiz.q: How do you create a new Landscape in a level?
choices: Drag a cube into the level and scale it up
Open Landscape Mode and choose New on the Manage tab
Open the Material Editor and add a Landscape Layer Blend node
Open Edit, then Plugins, and enable Landscape
new_quiz.explain: Landscape Mode has a Manage tab. Choosing New there creates a landscape with the size you set.

new_quiz.q: What can you use for the three layers in a first test if you have no ground textures yet?
choices: Three normal maps
Three landscapes
Three layer info objects
Three plain colors
new_quiz.explain: The layer blend works with any input. Three plain colors are enough to check that the layers paint as they should.

new_quiz.q: What is a decal?
choices: A mesh that is glued to a wall
A light that shines on one spot
A texture that fakes small bumps
A material that is projected onto surfaces
new_quiz.explain: A decal projects a material onto the surfaces inside its box, like a sticker or a stain.

new_quiz.q: What do decals let you add without making new meshes?
choices: Detail such as dirt, cracks or signs
Collision for the player
New rooms and floors
Shadows for the lights
new_quiz.explain: A decal lies on top of the surface that is already there. You get more detail and the meshes stay as they are.

new_quiz.q: Which setting turns a material into a decal material?
choices: Blend Mode set to Opaque
Material Domain set to Deferred Decal
Material Domain set to Surface
Shading Model set to Unlit
new_quiz.explain: The Material Domain tells Unreal what the material is used for. Deferred Decal is the domain for decals.

new_quiz.q: What is the decal box?
choices: The folder that stores decal materials
The mesh that the decal is painted on
The box that shows how far the decal projects
The window where you edit the decal
new_quiz.explain: The decal projects its material inside this box. Only surfaces inside the box receive the decal.

new_quiz.q: From where do you look at a decal to check if it is stretched?
choices: From a low angle
From straight above
From inside the wall
From the Material Editor
new_quiz.explain: Stretching shows best when you look along the surface. From straight on, a stretched decal can still look fine.

new_quiz.q: A decal looks stretched. What do you fix?
choices: The intensity of the nearest light
The Material Domain of the floor
The name of the decal material
The size of the decal box
new_quiz.explain: The decal is projected through its box. A box with the wrong size smears the material over the surface, so you correct the size.

new_quiz.q: Which three decals do you place in this quest?
choices: One on the floor, one on the sky and one on the player
One of grime, one stain and one directional marker
One red, one green and one blue
One large, one medium and one small
new_quiz.explain: Grime and a stain make surfaces look used. A directional marker, such as an arrow, shows that a decal can also give information.

new_quiz.q: What can a directional marker decal, such as an arrow, do for the player?
choices: Block a wrong route
Open a door
Point at a route
Light a dark room
new_quiz.explain: An arrow on the floor or wall leads the eye in one direction. It guides the player without any new geometry.
